$comment: How TransLink's routes are drawn where the GTFS alone doesn't say (packages/transit-core/DESIGN.md#routes). Every route in the feed is drawn by default, modelled from its GTFS route_type (buses: GTFS-RT with schedule fallback, category 'regular'; rail and ferries: along their shapes, 'rapid'), keyed by its short name without leading zeros ('025' → '25') or else its long name, labelled '<key> <long name>', in its GTFS route_color (#666666 without one). An entry here overrides any of that for the route it matches, by name (route_long_name / route_short_name, never route_id, which changes between feeds): 'kind' is how vehicles are modelled ('skytrain' = track-level, packages/transit-core/DESIGN.md#track-graph; 'shape' = interpolated along GTFS shapes; 'bus' = GTFS-RT with schedule fallback), 'kinematics' overrides the vehicle settings of the route's mode (config/defaults/kinematics.json, then its operator's), 'color' is the colour it's drawn in, and 'category' is its layer in the site's layers panel: 'rapid' (dedicated right of way: SkyTrain, SeaBus, West Coast Express), 'frequent' (the 99 B-Line and RapidBus R1–R6: frequent, but not true BRT, without dedicated right of way) or 'regular' (every other bus, drawn by frequency rather than in its own colour). Set by hand for now (the user's call, 2026-10-14); 'frequent' vs 'regular' should later be computed from scheduled frequency when the plan is built. The 99 is orange and every RapidBus the same green, as on TransLink's maps (the GTFS has other shades). 'exclude' leaves routes out of the plan altogether: not drawn, on cards or tracked.
